decisions.reason: The necessary cross-Requirement effect is already fully represented by the existing message-169 MODIFY, which records both the common-baseline rule for every letterform and the tighter optical-spacing exploration.

The common-baseline instruction changes complete-wordmark composition, not the construction or architectural design of the internal letterforms; the E and L letterform requirements remain valid unchanged.
Aligning the Hero V bottom point within the complete composition does not change its approved locked geometry; the source does not authorize redrawing or modifying the Hero V itself.
The source changes baseline placement and spacing but does not alter the É accent's derivation, vector-copy precision, peak alignment, or locked status.
Bottom-point baseline alignment does not change the shared Hero-V and É-accent terminal gesture or any terminal construction constraint.
The composition and baseline decision has no logically necessary effect on the deferred champagne-gold material treatment.
The baseline and kerning exploration implements the wordmark composition without changing the established brand character, positioning, or expression principles.
The source does not change the decision to use a proprietary wordmark without a separate icon or monogram.
